headline: In 1518 a city danced until people died.
slides: In Strasbourg, a woman known as Frau Troffea stepped into the street and began to dance. She couldn't stop.
Dozens had joined her. Within a month, by some counts, hundreds.
The city council thought more dancing would burn it out. They built a stage and hired musicians.
Dancers collapsed from exhaustion. Some reportedly died.
The worst afflicted were taken to a shrine of St Vitus. By September it was over.
Still debated. The leading theory is mass psychogenic illness after years of famine and disease.
